request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have dates and a person can have several; all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it behaves**
- **Leaving claims out:** a claim drops out of the live totals only if it is open (OPEN or PENDING), is dated within one of the person's holds, and is not bound by a statement. The totals affected are the person's, the sheet's, period close and statement taking. The person's other claims still count. Both the from-date and the to-date are inside the hold, and a hold with no to-date never ends.
- **Hold column:** it shows yes/no for whether the person has any hold at all, whatever the dates.
- **Audit:** holding writes `PERSON_HELD sheet=… by=… name=<name> from=<date>`, followed by the usual ROLLUP/TOTALS lines when the figures move. There is no release action any more, so `PERSON_RELEASED` is gone.

**What changed**
- **Data:** migration `V32__person_hold.sql` adds a `person_hold` table (person, from_date, to_date) and drops `person.held`. People who were held before this change get a hold with no dates, so they stay held for all their claims.
- **Server:**
  - New `PersonHold.java`.
  - `Person.counts(Claim)` now decides whether a claim counts. It replaces `ClaimStatus.counts(boolean held)` in the rollup, statement and period services.
  - `POST /{id}/hold` now takes `{from, to}`; a blank from-date means the sheet's today.
  - A to-date before the from-date is refused with `HoldDatesException`, which shows `person-error`. The tests don't cover that refusal.
  - The person data sent to the screen now includes the list of holds.
- **Screen (`people.ts`, `claims.ts`):** each person's row has `person-hold-from` and `person-hold-to` date fields, a Hold button (`person-hold-toggle`), and one `person-hold-line` per hold. The live totals on screen use the same rule as the server.

**Decision for you:** "bound by a statement" uses the app's existing `isBound` rule, which is stated and not PENDING. So a stated claim that is PENDING and dated within a hold drops out of the totals. If any stated claim should stay in, I'd check `stated` instead; the tests pass either way.
